title: Key-value storage: preferences, MMKV and UserDefaults

videos.script:
Every app keeps a few settings. {{settings}} The theme, the day the week starts, whether reminders are on. Each platform has a store for them, and they all have the same shape: names, small values, one file.

Today you write that store yourself, in a few lines of TypeScript. {{kv}} Writing it is how you see the one line that matters, the one that saves.

Because a phone kills apps without asking. {{torn}} If it happens while the file is being written, the next launch finds half a file. You will stop a save halfway on purpose, and watch the settings disappear. Then you fix it with a rename.

And you will measure the mistake everybody makes once. {{grow}} Keeping a list that grows in a preference. A thousand sessions, saved one at a time, write almost fifty megabytes to keep under a hundred kilobytes.
